title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
why_read: A skeptical re-examination of a recent claimed phenomenon in language models, showing a simpler explanation for the same empirical gains.
analysis: A prior paper claimed that pretrained language models sit in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts that random weight perturbations can reveal, dubbed the Neural Thickets hypothesis. This paper reproduces those performance gains but shows they can be explained more simply: perturbing outputs rather than weights, then selecting and voting among the results, gets the same or better results without touching the model's weights at all. That is a valuable scientific correction because it links the phenomenon to well-known ideas like self-consistency and ensemble voting rather than a new geometric property of weight space. This kind of debunking-with-a-simpler-model work is useful for keeping the field honest about what's actually driving reported improvements.
